subject: Basic Mathematics

questions.prompt: Express 0.11363636… as a fraction in its simplest form; only 36 recurs.
steps: Let p = 0.11363636… . Moving two and four decimal places gives 100p = 11.363636… and 10,000p = 1136.363636… .
Subtract to cancel the recurring tail: 9900p = 1125. Thus p = 1125/9900 = 5/44.
questions.tip: The two initial 1s do not repeat. Keep the recurring block aligned before subtracting.

questions.prompt: Write 0.00070482 to three significant figures.
steps: Start counting significant digits at the first nonzero digit: 7,0,4. The following digit is 8.
Round 704 up to 705, keeping the original decimal position.

questions.prompt: Round 1,233,388 to the nearest ten thousand.
steps: The ten-thousands digit is 3; the following thousands digit is 3.
Since the following digit is below 5, retain the ten-thousands digit and replace all smaller places with zero.

questions.prompt: Three-fifths of Tanzania’s people live in cities in the stated model. What percentage does not live in cities?
steps: The complement is 1 − 3/5 = 2/5.
Convert to a percentage: (2/5) × 100 = 40%.

questions.prompt: Express 27ⁿ × 9²ⁿ × 3 as a single power of 3.
steps: 27ⁿ = (3³)ⁿ = 3³ⁿ and 9²ⁿ = (3²)²ⁿ = 3⁴ⁿ.
When multiplying powers with the same base, add exponents: 3n + 4n + 1 = 7n + 1.

questions.prompt: Rationalise the denominator of (√2 + 1)/(√2 − √5).
steps: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate √2 + √5.
The denominator becomes 2 − 5 = −3. Expanding the numerator gives 2 + √10 + √2 + √5. Divide by −3.

questions.prompt: Given log₁₀2 = 0.3010 and log₁₀3 = 0.4771, find log₁₀72.
steps: Factor 72 = 2³ × 3². Apply the product and power rules: log72 = 3log2 + 2log3.

questions.prompt: Of 260 students, 130 take Physics, 150 Chemistry and 40 both. How many take Physics only?
steps: The Physics total includes those taking both subjects.
Subtract the overlap: 130 − 40 = 90.

questions.prompt: How many of those students take neither subject?
steps: Union = 130 + 150 − 40 = 240. The overlap is subtracted because it was counted twice.
Neither = total − union = 260 − 240 = 20.

questions.prompt: Among 35 livestock keepers, 18 keep goats, 20 cows and 3 both. Draw a Venn diagram and find P(goats only).
questions.answer: Goats only 15; both 3; cows only 17; neither 0. P(goats only) = 3/7.
steps: Place 3 in the intersection. Goats only = 18 − 3 = 15; cows only = 20 − 3 = 17.
Union = 15 + 3 + 17 = 35, so none lie outside both circles. Favourable keepers = 15; probability = 15/35 = 3/7.

questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, exterior angle ABD = 150° and area = 22.6 cm². Find BC.
steps: Interior ∠ABC = 180° − 150° = 30°. Use area = ½ AB × BC × sin∠ABC.
22.6 = ½ × 8 × BC × ½ = 2BC. Therefore BC = 22.6/2 = 11.3 cm.

questions.prompt: Find the perimeter of a regular pentagon inscribed in a circle of radius 10 m.
steps: Each central angle is 360°/5 = 72°. Bisecting one isosceles triangle gives a right triangle with angle 36° and hypotenuse 10 m.
Half a side = 10sin36°, so a side = 20sin36°. Multiply by five sides: perimeter = 100sin36°.

questions.prompt: Using the stated exchange rate Tsh 2300 per US dollar, convert Tsh 27,600,000 to dollars.
steps: One dollar costs Tsh 2300, so divide the shilling amount by 2300.

questions.prompt: Cylinder height varies directly as volume and inversely as radius squared. Height 3 cm corresponds to volume 900 cm³ and radius 10 cm. Find height for 1200 cm³ and radius 5 cm.
steps: Write h = kV/r². Substitute the first conditions: 3 = k × 900/100 = 9k, so k = 1/3.
For the new cylinder, h = (1/3)(1200)/25 = 400/25 = 16 cm.

questions.prompt: For a = 2i − j, b = −i + 3j and c = 3i − 4j, find the magnitude of a + b + c.
steps: Add corresponding components: a + b + c = (2 − 1 + 3)i + (−1 + 3 − 4)j = 4i − 2j.

questions.prompt: A line segment has midpoint (3,5) and one endpoint (6,7). Find the other endpoint.
steps: Let the missing endpoint be (x,y). The midpoint formula gives (6 + x)/2 = 3 and (7 + y)/2 = 5.
Thus x = 6 − 6 = 0 and y = 10 − 7 = 3. Check the averages are (3,5).

questions.prompt: Sand, gravel and cement are mixed in ratio 500:600:200. How much cement is in 39,000 kg of mixture?
steps: Total ratio parts = 500 + 600 + 200 = 1300. Cement contributes 200/1300 of the mixture.

questions.prompt: Opening stock Tsh 2000, purchases 13,000, closing stock 500, sales 30,000 and expenses 6500: find net profit.
steps: Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases − closing stock = 2000 + 13,000 − 500 = 14,500.
Gross profit = sales − cost of goods sold = 30,000 − 14,500 = 15,500.
Net profit = gross profit − expenses = 15,500 − 6500 = 9000.

questions.prompt: Calculate the amount after investing Tsh 10,000 at 5% compound interest per year for three years.
steps: For annual compounding, A = P(1 + r)ⁿ with P = 10,000, r = 0.05 and n = 3.

questions.prompt: The numbers 3, x − 1 and 27 form a geometric progression. Find x.
steps: For consecutive GP terms, the middle term squared equals first × third: (x − 1)² = 3 × 27 = 81.
x − 1 = ±9, so x = 10 or −8. Check the sequences 3,9,27 and 3,−9,27 have ratios 3 and −3 respectively.
questions.tip: A geometric progression can have a negative common ratio. Retain both solutions unless a positive ratio is required.

questions.prompt: Find the largest angle in a triangle with side lengths 6,7 and 8 cm.
steps: The largest angle is opposite the longest side, 8 cm. Apply the cosine rule: 8² = 6² + 7² − 2(6)(7)cosθ.

questions.prompt: ABC is right-angled at B, with AC = 6 cm and AB = 3 cm. Find tan∠C.
steps: AC is the hypotenuse. By Pythagoras, BC = √(6² − 3²) = √27 = 3√3.
Relative to angle C, the opposite side is AB and the adjacent side is BC. Therefore tanC = 3/(3√3) = √3/3.

questions.prompt: Given x = 1/t⁵, rewrite 2/t¹⁰ − 3/t⁵ + 1 = 0 in terms of x.
steps: Since x = t⁻⁵, x² = t⁻¹⁰. The original equation requires t ≠ 0.
Replace 1/t¹⁰ with x² and 1/t⁵ with x.

questions.prompt: Solve the resulting quadratic 2x² − 3x + 1 = 0.
steps: Set each factor to zero: 2x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1/2; x − 1 = 0 gives x = 1. If t is also needed, t = 1 or ⁵√2.

questions.prompt: Marks 65–69,70–74,75–79,80–84,85–89,90–94 have frequencies 10,12,55,10,5,8. How many pupils scored 75–79?
steps: Find the class interval 75–79 in the table.
Its frequency is 55. Frequencies count pupils; do not use the class midpoint or cumulative total.

questions.prompt: Calculate the grouped median of the marks to the nearest whole number.
steps: Total N = 100; cumulative frequencies are 10,22,77,87,92,100. N/2 = 50 lies in the 75–79 class.
Use continuous lower boundary L = 74.5, preceding cumulative frequency 22, class frequency 55 and width 5.
Median = 74.5 + [(50 − 22)/55] × 5 = 77.04545… . Round to the nearest whole mark: 77.

questions.prompt: Find the distance between X(60°N,30°E) and Y(60°N,40°E), taking a degree at the equator as 111.6 km.
questions.answer: 558 km along the parallel of latitude.
steps: Longitude difference = 40° − 30° = 10°. At latitude 60°, the parallel’s radius is the equatorial radius multiplied by cos60° = 1/2.
Distance along that parallel = 10 × 111.6 × 1/2 = 558 km.
questions.tip: This is the parallel-arc distance requested by the latitude model, rather than a great-circle route.

questions.prompt: A closed rectangular box has dimensions 40 cm by 30 cm by 50 cm. Find its space diagonal AG.
steps: The base diagonal squared is 40² + 30² = 2500.
The space diagonal squared adds the height squared: AG² = 2500 + 50² = 5000. Therefore AG = √5000 = 50√2.

questions.prompt: Find the outside surface area of the closed box.
questions.answer: 9400 cm² for all six outer faces.
steps: There are two faces of each size: 40 × 30, 40 × 50 and 30 × 50.
questions.tip: If “the sides” is restricted to the four vertical faces, their lateral area is 2(40 + 30) × 50 = 7000 cm². The complete closed-box outside area includes its top and bottom.

questions.prompt: G = [[−1,11],[a,3]] is singular. Find a.
steps: A singular square matrix has determinant zero. detG = (−1)(3) − 11a = −3 − 11a.
Set −3 − 11a = 0, giving a = −3/11.

questions.prompt: Use a matrix method to solve 5x + 3y = 9 and 10x + 7y = 11.
Given f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = 3x − 2, find the product of f⁻¹(x) and g⁻¹(x).
steps: To invert f, write y = x + 2 and solve x = y − 2: f⁻¹(x) = x − 2. To invert g, y = 3x − 2 gives g⁻¹(x) = (x + 2)/3.
Multiply the inverse values: (x − 2)(x + 2)/3 = (x² − 4)/3.
questions.tip: The paper asks for the product of the inverse functions. A product multiplies their values; a composition would substitute one function into the other.

questions.prompt: A tailor has 150 m² cotton and 90 m² wool. A suit needs 1 m² cotton and 2 m² wool; a gown needs 3 m² cotton and 1 m² wool. Revenues are Tsh 40,000 per suit and 60,000 per gown. Formulate the revenue-maximising problem.
questions.answer: Maximise Z = 40,000x + 60,000y, subject to x + 3y ≤ 150; 2x + y ≤ 90; x,y ≥ 0, with x,y whole numbers.
steps: Let x be the number of suits and y the number of gowns. Cotton used = x + 3y and wool used = 2x + y.
Usage cannot exceed available cloth, so both constraints use ≤. Multiply each garment count by its revenue to form the objective. Nonnegative whole numbers reflect garment counts.

summaries.Section A — Worked solutions: Align recurring decimals before subtracting. Complements and Venn diagrams avoid double counting; ratios and variation equations must use consistent units.
summaries.Section B — Worked solutions: Use class boundaries for grouped medians. A space diagonal includes all three squared dimensions. Inverse functions, products and matrix inverses are different operations.

labelling_note: Question 12(b)(ii) includes the complete outside area of the closed box and identifies the alternative lateral-area reading of “sides”.
